"PROJECT: ULTIMATE OPEN WORLD – MOBILE 3D RACING GAME

Act as a world-class AAA game development studio consisting of expert 3D environment artists, vehicle designers, game programmers, physics engineers, UI/UX designers and optimization specialists.

Your task is to CREATE a complete, playable, highly detailed, realistic 3D open-world car driving and racing game for Android mobile devices.

The game should deliver an experience comparable in ambition, freedom, visual quality and exploration to the Forza Horizon series, while having its own original identity.

Do not create a simple demo, basic prototype, low-poly driving simulator or static environment. Build a genuinely explorable 3D game.

1. MASSIVE OPEN WORLD MAP

Create an extremely large, seamless open-world map containing multiple geographically different regions.

The world must include:

- Modern metropolitan cities with skyscrapers.
- Beautiful residential areas and suburbs.
- Small towns and villages.
- Long highways with multiple lanes.
- Mountain ranges with winding roads.
- Snow-covered mountains and snowy roads.
- Deserts with sand dunes.
- Green forests and dense vegetation.
- Beautiful countryside and farmland.
- Coastal highways beside the ocean.
- Beaches and seaside towns.
- Rivers, lakes and waterfalls.
- Bridges, tunnels and underground roads.
- Industrial areas, factories and ports.
- Racing circuits and professional race tracks.
- Off-road trails and rocky terrain.

All regions should connect naturally through roads and highways.

The map should feel alive, enormous and worth exploring. Avoid repetitive buildings, repeated scenery and empty landscapes.

2. HUGE CAR COLLECTION

Include a massive collection of selectable and drivable vehicles.

Vehicle categories:

- Hypercars
- Supercars
- Sports cars
- Luxury sedans
- SUVs
- Off-road vehicles
- Pickup trucks
- Muscle cars
- Classic cars
- Electric vehicles
- Racing cars
- Drift cars
- Rally cars
- Vans
- Buses

Include vehicles inspired by real-world automotive designs, with original or properly licensed models.

Every vehicle must have:

- Highly detailed 3D exterior.
- Realistic body proportions.
- Detailed headlights and taillights.
- Realistic wheels, tyres and rims.
- Detailed windows and glass reflections.
- Realistic paint and metallic materials.
- Working brake lights and indicators.
- Realistic suspension movement.
- Visible steering-wheel movement.
- Realistic acceleration and braking.
- Different engine sounds.
- Different handling characteristics.

Each vehicle must feel unique.

A hypercar should be extremely fast, while an SUV should have different handling and suspension characteristics.

3. VEHICLE SWITCHING SYSTEM

Create a beautiful 3D garage where players can:

- Browse a huge collection of cars.
- Select and switch vehicles instantly.
- Rotate cars and inspect them from every angle.
- View vehicle specifications.
- Customize paint colours.
- Change wheels and rims.
- Add spoilers and body modifications.
- Upgrade engine, brakes and suspension.
- Save favourite vehicles.

Allow players to switch between unlocked cars without restarting the game.

4. ULTRA-REALISTIC GRAPHICS

Visual quality is one of the highest priorities.

Use advanced graphics techniques wherever supported:

- High-quality PBR materials.
- Realistic car reflections.
- Detailed vehicle textures.
- Realistic shadows.
- Dynamic lighting.
- Ambient occlusion.
- Realistic glass materials.
- Detailed road textures.
- High-quality vegetation.
- Realistic water rendering.
- Volumetric lighting where supported.
- Beautiful sunsets and sunrises.
- Realistic clouds and sky.
- High-quality environmental details.

Cars must look like professionally modelled automotive 3D assets, not toy cars or basic geometric shapes.

Environments must have realistic depth, lighting, textures and scale.

5. REALISTIC DRIVING PHYSICS

Implement a proper vehicle physics system.

Include:

- Realistic acceleration.
- Different top speeds.
- Realis

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"
